topic: Exact counts of primes with literal binomial remainders different from the positive integer n
title: Exact counts and sharp growth for OEIS A222759, first comment (12 March 2013): extending Glaisher (1900)

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Glaisher's (1900) congruence to exact literal-remainder counts, we determine OEIS A222759 and prove Noe's growth assertion in its first comment (12 March 2013; revision 12, 2 November 2024). For every positive integer n, its conjectured count equals pi(floor(n^(1/3))) plus two explicit corrections supported below 27. Consequently, for every k >= 3, the count is at least k exactly when n >= p_k^3, sharpening the stated sufficient threshold p_(p_k^3). The same description determines A222760, including its exceptional relation to A222759 at n=5. We give a self-contained proof, the counts modulo p and p^2, and elementary consequences for the linked prime-counting entries.
summary: The bad primes are precisely those with p^3 <= n, together with 2 if n < 8 and n mod 4 is 2 or 3, and 3 if n < 27 and n mod 3 is 2. Thus a(n) >= k iff n >= p_k^3 for k >= 3. The companion b(n) equals p_(a(n)+1) except at n=5, where b(5)=5. Written corollaries give the small count levels, linked elementary interpretations, generating functions and prime-number-theorem consequences.
